title: Subdural Soft Electrocorticography (ECoG) Array Implantation and Long-Term Cortical Recording in Minipigs
protocol: Record the voltage drop upon injection of a biphasic current pulse using an oscilloscope connected in parallel to a pulse generator.
Connect the pulse generator sequentially to each electrode and a platinum counter in saline solution (PBS 1x).
Measure the electrochemical impedance at different frequencies using a potentiometer.
Connect the potentiometer sequentially to each electrode using the platinum counter and an Ag/AgCl reference electrode in saline solution (PBS 1x).
In the dry state, measure the direct current resistance between adjacent channels using a handheld multimeter.
Select the implant with impedance at 1 kHz below 100 kΩ and no inter-channel resistance below 1 MΩ.
Place the selected implants individually into sterilization bags along with a sterilization marker and seal them.
Employ double packaging to ensure sterility during surgery.
Premedicate the animal by isolating it and fasting it overnight.
Inject a mix of midazolam at 0.75 mg/kg, atropine at 0.25 µg/kg, and haldol at 0.1 mg/kg intradermally.
Wait until the animal is sedated before proceeding.
Weigh the animal.
Place the animal on the surgery table on a heating pad.
Induce anesthesia by placing a face mask on the animal using sevoflurane at 3%-3.5%.
Place electrocardiogram leads on the abdomen.
Place a blood saturation sensor on the tail.
Insert a temperature sensor in the nostril.
Place an IV lead on an ear vein and confirm blood access with a syringe filled with saline.
Keep the eyes hydrated by using ointment during surgery.
Inject a bolus of atracurium at 0.5 mg/kg, ketamine at 1 mg/kg, and fentanyl at 1-2 µg/kg.
Place the animal on its back for intubation.
Insert a 4.5 mm tube.
Stop the sevoflurane anesthesia after intubation.
Install a propofol infusion at 10 mg/kg/h.
Install an fentanyl infusion at 2 µg/kg/h.
Install an atracurium infusion at 0.2-0.5 mg/kg/h.
Install a saline infusion at 4-7 mg/kg/h.
Start an infusion of mannitol at 1 g/kg/h to reduce brain swelling during the surgery.
Place the animal on its abdomen in the sphinx position for x-ray acquisition.
Temporarily remove any metallic object near the brain and skull of the animal.
Acquire an axial and sagittal plane x-ray with a contrast of the bone.
Place a metallic object with known dimensions in the sagittal acquisition field as a scale.
Identify the location of the frontal sinuses visible by voids below the skull.
Mark the most posterior location on the head using a permanent marker.
Shave the entire surface of the head beyond the surgical field.
Thoroughly scrub the head with betadine using a sterile pad.
Place sterile drapes on the instrumentation table and on the animal, revealing only the surgical window.
Scrub the head again with a sterile pad using betadine.
Incise the skin along the midline with a scalpel knife.
Separate muscle and periosteum from bone using a raspatory.
Identify bregma and lambda, and mark them with a sterile surgical pen.
Define the bone flap outline centered around the implantation target on both hemispheres.
Drill the outline of the craniotomy using a bone drill with a round cutting bit.
Irrigate the drilling location with saline solution to avoid overheating of the bone.
Carefully drill the outline homogeneously until reaching the dura mater.
At the first breakthrough, continue drilling to thin the bone flap enough to almost break through.
Use a flat spatula on either the midline side or lateral side to break away the bone flap in one piece using the craniotomy edge as leverage.
If resistance is encountered, continue thinning the bone until it can be removed easily.
Place the removed bone piece in sterile saline.
Carefully chip the edge of the craniotomy with a Kerison to avoid sharp edges from cutting into the dura mater.
Use Gelfoam or bone wax if excessive bleeding occurs on the dura mater or bone, respectively.
Place a wet compress (standard pad in sterile saline solution) in the craniotomy.
Repeat this step on the other hemisphere.
Using the needle from a 6-0 suture kit, carefully pierce and lift the dura mater at the anterior or posterior end of the craniotomy halfway between the medial and lateral side.
Create the beginning of an incision with the stab knife.
Create an anteroposterior slit in the dura mater larger than the width of the implant.
Cover any bleeding with gel foam and wait until it stops.
Irrigate the implant with saline on both sides to facilitate sliding into the subdural space.
Place the implant above the dura mater slit.
Insert the device subdurally by sliding it sequentially on each edge with small forceps.
Hold the pedestal end of the device carefully while advancing it to avoid creating tension.
Stop insertion when the connector edge is located on top of the slit.
Place a titanium bridge over the cable after the craniotomy or in the anchoring wings.
Secure the implant using one or two titanium screws with an appropriate screwdriver.
Remove 1 cm of insulation from the ground wires carefully.
Insert the ground wire epidurally at the posterior end of the craniotomy.
Repeat steps for contra-lateral hemisphere.
Place a wet pad over the surgery location with sterile saline solution.
Cover the head of the animal with a sterile surgery drape.
Take axial x-ray images to confirm implant placement.
Take sagittal x-ray images to confirm implant placement.
Remove the drape and explant the device if not correctly placed.
Reinsert the device following steps 2.4.4. and 2.5.1.-2.5.3 again.
Suture the dura mater carefully around the implant cable using a 3-0 resorbable suture.
Fix titanium bridges on the anterior and posterior part of each bone flap with titanium screws.
Secure the end of the titanium bridges to the skull.
Position the footplate on the skull to optimize screw placement.
Skip holes in the legs if screws cannot be screwed in.
Screw in the titanium screws until the footplate is firmly in place.
Remove the titanium bridges over the connection cables and flip over the pedestal.
Land the pedestal on the footplate and screw it securely onto the footplate.
Clean the subcutaneous space of any bone or debris by flushing with saline.
Cut away skin around the pedestal edges to create a round edge following the cylinder.
Fold the skin flaps together after removing the spreaders.
Create subcutaneous sutures using a 4-0 non-resorbable suture wire, 3 mm apart, starting from away from the pedestal and moving toward it on both sides of the incision.
Suture the skin using a 6-0 non-resorbable suture wire, with sutures 5 mm apart, starting from away from the pedestal and moving toward it on both sides of the incision.
Clean the wound area again with a sterile pad and betadine.
Apply a self-adhesive sterile bandage over the wound.
Take the animal off all anesthetics but keep under ventilation after measurements are performed.
Apply a buprenorphine patch (25 mg/h) for 24 h for analgesia.
Place the animal on a heating pad covered with drapes to speed up wake-up time.
Extubate the animal when spontaneous breathing is recovered.
Put the animal under an oxygen face mask until consciousness is recovered.
Keep the animal under close surveillance for 5 days postoperatively.
Give a dose of cephalexin at 75 mg twice daily with food, separated from other animals.
Disinfect the wound daily by applying copious amounts of betadine with soaked sterile pads during feeding.
Record the voltage drop upon injection of a biphasic current pulse using an oscilloscope.
Connect the pulse generator sequentially to each electrode and the ground wire.
Perform the stimulation pulse at 100 µA with a pulse width of 300 µs at 100 Hz.
Measure the electrochemical impedance at different frequencies using a potentiometer.
Set the excitation voltage to 200 mV and the frequency range from 1 Hz to 1 MHz, with three points per decade.
Connect the pulse generator sequentially to each electrode, using the ground wire as both the counter electrode and the ground.
Measure the DC resistance between adjacent channels using a handheld multimeter.
Plug the wireless recording system through the pedestal and record baseline activity for 2-3 min.
Insert speakers in a closed field in the animal ears.
Play tone burst acoustic stimulation at different frequencies (ranging from 200-20,000 Hz) at around 70 dB SPL over 120 repetitions.
Average the recordings and align them over the stimulus period for analysis.
Place needles in the snout at three different positions.
Evoke sensory potentials by stimulating the snout for ~30 s with the pulse generator at different amplitudes to obtain recruitment curves.
Keep the animal under propofol anesthesia.
Use a transport cart that houses a ventilator, syringe pump, and vital signs monitor to transport the animal from the surgery room to the imaging facilities and back.
Place the animal on the scanner table.
Remove any metallic object around the head (e.g., the temperature sensor).
Acquire a CT scan at the smallest resolution (0.4 mm slice thickness) using isometric acquisition with automatic current and voltage selection for bone contrast.
Remove all equipment containing metal from the animal.
Ventilate and anesthetize the animal under sevoflurane at 3%-3.5% using a ventilator situated outside the MRI chamber.
Inject a bolus of fentanyl at 1-2 μg/kg before the first sequence.
Use three isometric sequences at the smallest resolution: T1-, T2-, and turbo spin echo (TSE)-weighted sequences.
Follow the procedure described in section 4 for recording awake signals from the brain.
Plug the wireless headstage by holding the animal or feeding it with treats to distract it.
Provide acoustic stimulation using external speakers placed close to the animal.
Insert a catheter into the carotid artery if perfusion is required.
Dissect the skin and muscle along the midline of the throat, following the middle white line (no vessels underneath).
Cut the carotid artery and jugular vein for dissection.
Open the area using fingers to make space around the trachea and under the muscle.
Look for the carotid artery, which is beating and pinkish.
Identify the vagal nerve if present, appearing white.
Locate the jugular vein underneath or on the side, which appears red.
Place spreaders as shown in Supplementary Figure 2B.
Start dissecting the carotid artery using fine forceps and round scissors.
Use scissors to open conjunctive tissue.
If no blood vessels are present, cut; if blood vessels are present, cauterize and move forward (Supplementary Figures 2C, D).
When sufficient dissection is achieved, use a clamp to go underneath the carotid artery for complete isolation (Supplementary Figure 2E).
Repeat the same operation with the jugular vein (Supplementary Figure 2F).
Place suture wire around both vessels when fully dissected and isolated.
Do not close them yet.
Place two sutures around the carotid artery: one at the very base (suture 1, heart side for brain perfusion) and another on the other side (suture 2) as shown in Supplementary Figure 2G.
Place one suture around the jugular vein (suture 3), but do not close it yet; mark the wires with tape for later sectioning of the vein.
Close suture 1 very firmly to prevent bleeding, tying three knots (Supplementary Figure 2H).
Place a clamp on the wire to put weight and create tension in the carotid artery.
Clamp the carotid artery using a vessel clamp on the opposite side of the dissection.
Catch and pull the carotid artery with black forceps.
Section half of the carotid artery near the base of the dissection using fine scissors.
Insert the catheter into the sectioned area.
Flush the catheter with PBS to remove any air.
Close suture 2 firmly enough for the catheter to move slightly.
Remove the vessel clamp and insert the catheter as far as possible.
Finalize the closure of suture 2 securely.
Attach the base of the catheter to the skin at the exit of the wound using suture wires if desired.
Transfer the animal to the perfusion zone and connect it to PBS/heparin.
Pull suture 3 and cut the jugular vein when the perfusion starts.
Deliver pentobarbital (90 mg/kg) intravenously.
Flush the line with saline to ensure full dose administration.
Plug the carotid catheter into PBS/heparin (1 L for a 15 kg pig).
Switch to PBS containing 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) (5 L for a 15 kg pig).
Pull suture 3 and cut the jugular vein when perfusion starts.
Detach the animal's head from the body using a scalpel, cutting through skin and muscle.
Insert the blade between the first and second vertebrae to behead the animal.
Plunge the head in 4% PFA in PBS for 48 hours at 4°C.
Transfer the head to PBS after postfixation.
Remove the skin from the head using a scalpel.
Cut the bone carefully starting from the first vertebrae using a rongeur, following the spinal cord to the cerebellum.
Expose and remove the temporal bones to expose the parietal and frontal lobes.
Screw off the pedestal from the footplate.
Cut the feet of the footplate with pliers.
Remove bone near the cable entry into the skull to free the implant system without pulling implants out.
If cables are embedded in bone, cut them as close as possible to the exit point.
Carefully cut the dura following the midline using small scissors.
Free the implant cables from the dura mater exit.
Take photographs of the implant placement on the brain.
Use a small spoon to detach the brain from the cranial nerves below.
Carefully extract the brain.
Remove the implants from the brain.
Postfix the extracted brain for 24 h in 4% PFA in PBS at 4 °C if needed based on perfusion quality.
Store the brain in 0.1 M PBS at 4 °C until cutting.
Separate the two hemispheres using a razor blade.
Cut the brain orthogonally into four pieces.
Cut the implanted zone in half to obtain blocks containing the implanted and control areas.
Transfer the brain blocks to a solution of 15% sucrose first, then to 30% sucrose at 4 °C until equilibrium is reached.
Freeze the tissue in isopentane at -55 °C using a tissue freezing system.
Place the frozen brain in a cryostat and trim until full sections are achieved.
Slice the brain into 40 µm sections.
Immerse the sections in groups of three in 0.1 M PBS in well plates.
Carefully note the order of the plates.
Select the sections depending on the zone to analyze.
Inspect the sections for damage with a fine brush.
Place the sections in new well plates filled with 0.1 M PBS.
Incubate the sections in 0.3% Triton X/PBS for 15 min at room temperature.
Incubate the sections in 3% bovine serum albumin (BSA)/PBS for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash the wells with 0.1 M PBS three times for 5 min each.
Incubate the tissues with primary antibodies diluted in 1% BSA/PBS for 48 h at room temperature.
Cover the well plates with aluminum foil during incubation with primary antibodies.
Incubate the tissues with secondary antibodies diluted in 1% BSA/PBS for 2 h at room temperature.
Incubate the tissues with DAPI (1/1,000 in 1% BSA/PBS) for 15 min.
Wash the wells with 0.1 M PBS five times for 15 min each.
Mount the slides using mounting media and a coverslip.
Keep the slides in the dark at 4 °C.
Image the slides at 10x magnification using a slide scanner microscope at three different wavelengths (640 nm, 560 nm, 485 nm).
Image the region of interest at 20x magnification using a confocal microscope.
Use four wavelengths for imaging: Alexa Fluor 647, DAPI, Cy3, and EGFP.
